guidance:
You have ByteAsk grounded-reference tools that return VERBATIM, PAGE-CITED excerpts from authoritative specifications:
- autosar_ref — C/C++ coding standards & language specs (MISRA C/C++, AUTOSAR C++14, C++ Core Guidelines, ISO C++, C11): rule ids, 'is X allowed/compliant', rationale, language clauses.
- mcu_ref — embedded silicon & firmware (STM32/ESP32/Cortex-M registers, Modbus, CAN/ISO-TP, MQTT, linker scripts).
- fpga_ref — AMD/Xilinx FPGA (UG/PG guides, Vivado/Vitis, GT attributes, AXI/PCIe/DDR4 IP).
- hft_ref — exchange & network wire protocols (ITCH/OUCH/FIX/PITCH, RFC IP/TCP/UDP, PTP, SFP/QSFP).
- grid_ref — grid/DER standards (IEEE 1547/2030.5, SunSpec, G98/G99, grid codes).
- scpi_ref — SCPI test & measurement instrument command references.
- x86_ref — the full Intel x86 SDM (MSRs, CPUID, opcodes, paging, memory ordering).

Before stating any such detail from memory — a coding-standard rule, a register/bitfield/reset value, a protocol field offset, an MSR, an SCPI command, a trip threshold — call the matching tool and quote the cited result; these specifics are exactly what language models get wrong. Call a *_ref tool only when the task involves its domain or the user asks, not by default on general C/C++ work (this overrides the 'proactively' in autosar_ref's description).

COMBINE grounded lookups with web_search for the best answer:
- The *_ref tools are the SOURCE OF TRUTH for exact, safety-critical values (rule compliance, register/reset values, wire field offsets, MSRs) — prefer their page-cited excerpt over web or memory.
- web_search adds breadth: newer material, library/idiom usage, and the long tail these corpora only sample. When a *_ref tool replies 'no confident match' the topic is NOT in the corpus: for a long-tail part (an un-indexed MCU/FPGA/instrument/regional code) follow up with a site:-scoped web_search of the vendor/standard and LABEL it web-sourced (verify against the datasheet); for an exact authoritative miss (a rule id, MSR, or field offset) tell the user it is not covered rather than presenting a web guess as fact.

Use ref_context to expand a hit's `_ref:` id to its full section, and ref_request to log a document that is genuinely missing. Never silently answer a spec detail from memory.

tools.description: Expand a reference search hit to its full section. Pass the `_ref:` id returned by any *_ref search tool (autosar_ref, mcu_ref, fpga_ref, hft_ref, grid_ref, scpi_ref, x86_ref). Use when a returned snippet is truncated or you need the surrounding clauses / adjacent fields / the whole table.
tools.name: ref_context

ref_id.description: The `_ref:` id from a prior *_ref search hit whose full section you want.

tools.description: Record a request for a document ByteAsk has NOT indexed. Use ONLY after a *_ref search returned 'no confident match' AND the user genuinely needs that spec indexed. Pass a short free-text description (title / standard / version). This does NOT answer anything — it logs the gap so the document can be added later.
tools.name: ref_request

request.description: Short free-text description of the missing document (title / standard / version).

tools.description: Search 33 AMD/Xilinx + interconnect references and return VERBATIM, page-cited excerpts: UltraScale GTH/GTY/GTM (UG576/UG578/UG581), 7-series GTX (UG476), SelectIO/clocking (UG571/UG471/UG572), Vivado constraints/synth/impl/methodology (UG903/UG901/UG904/UG949), Vitis HLS (UG1399), Versal (AM011), device datasheets (DS922/DS923/DS182); LogiCORE IP — 10G/25G+100G Ethernet (PG210/PG203), PCIe (PG213/PG156), XDMA/QDMA/AXI-DMA (PG195/PG302/PG021), DDR4 (PG150), PCS/PMA, AXI Interconnect/Stream; plus AMBA AXI/ACE (IHI0022H), AXI4-Stream (IHI0051B), PCIe Base 4.0. Call it for GT attributes/DRP maps/defaults, XDC syntax, HLS pragmas, IP register maps, AXI signals & response codes (TKEEP, BRESP/DECERR), or TLP formats — never guess an attribute default. Coverage is AMD/Xilinx-centric: for Intel/Altera/Lattice parts or an un-indexed UG/PG a 'no confident match' is expected — then use web_search site:docs.amd.com / the vendor's site to cover the long tail.

This corpus indexes a curated SET of parts, not every MCU: if the exact part (e.g. an STM32H7, nRF52, RP2040) returns 'no confident match', that part is not indexed — then use web_search site:st.com / site:espressif.com / the vendor's site for the datasheet, and label it as web-sourced (verify against the datasheet). Never invent a register or reset value.

tools.description: Search the complete Intel 64 / IA-32 Software Developer's Manual, Vols 1-4 (5,342 pages, doc 325462) and return VERBATIM, page-cited excerpts. Call it for MSR names/addresses (e.g. IA32_TSC_DEADLINE = 6E0H), CPUID leaves & feature bits, CR0-CR4 bits, instruction semantics/opcodes/flag effects, paging structures, the memory-ordering model, or APIC/TSC/VMX detail — before quoting any from memory. This is the authoritative x86 reference: a 'no confident match' means it is not in the SDM — tell the user; do NOT quote a web-guessed MSR address or opcode as fact (for a quick opcode cross-check, web_search site:felixcloutier.com and label it).

tools.description: Search the full text of the C/C++ safety & coding standards and return VERBATIM, page-cited excerpts: AUTOSAR C++14 (all 397 rules), MISRA C++:2008 (all 228 rules), MISRA C:2012, the C++ Core Guidelines, ISO C++ (N4950) and C11 (N1570). Call this BEFORE stating any coding-standard or language-standard fact from memory (they are frequently misremembered), and PROACTIVELY while writing or reviewing C/C++: for any rule id (A5-2-2, M0-1-1, 0-1-1, Dir 4.6, ES.20 — type them plain, en-dashes optional), 'is X allowed / compliant', a rule's rationale/exceptions/examples, or a language clause (UB, lifetime, conversions, templates). Follow the rule it returns and cite the id. Core Guidelines cite by §section, not page. This corpus IS the authoritative rulebook: a 'no confident match' means the rule/topic is genuinely not covered (e.g. SEI CERT C++ is not indexed) — tell the user and do NOT answer a rule-compliance question from memory or a web guess. For modern library/idiom usage (not a rule), use web_search site:cppreference.com instead.
